E. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

MPLX and its business partner continue to work toward improved coordination of process safety information and MOC implementation improvements focusing on procedures that mesh into both parties management systems.  The Terminal and MPLX actively seek employee input to improve system process safety.  All process safety events (incidents) as defined in API 754 are recorded/tracked electronically, reviewed, and/or investigated via root cause analysis (ex. TapRooT) per corporate policy.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RELEASE POLICIES

MPLX Terminals LLC (MPLX) - North Muskegon LP Terminal is a refined petroleum products distributor. The North Muskegon Terminal is an onshore, light products, bulk petroleum storage terminal used in the storage and distribution of petroleum products to retail and commercial end-users in the vicinity of North Muskegon, MI. The Terminal handles and stores various grades of unleaded gasoline, low-sulfur diesel, butane, ethanol, and various other petroleum-based additives.

The North Muskegon LP Terminal is committed to operating and maintaining processes in a safe, reliable and environmentally sound manner. MPLX believes that excellent performance in health, safety, and the environment goes hand in hand with operating reliably, and that outstanding HES performance is of paramount importance.

The North Muskegon Terminal is designed, operated and maintained in a manner that protects the environment, as well as the health and safety of its employees, contractors and the community. MPLX promotes health, safety, and the environment through programs of awareness, compliance, prevention and protection. These programs include a combination of accidental release prevention and emergency response planning. This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that MPLX has designed and implemented, including:

A. A description of the facility and the use of regulated substances;
B. An overview of the accidental release prevention programs (Program Level 3);
C. A five-year accident history for accidental releases of regulated chemicals;
D. An overview of the emergency response program; and
E. An overview of planned changes to improve process safety.

A. STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Butane Blending process has been classified as Program Level 3.  No Program 1 or 2 processes are identified. By virtue of the flammable effects associated with butane, it is necessary to

observe certain safety precautions to prevent unnecessary human exposure, to reduce the threat and impacts to employee health and nearby members of the community along with the surrounding environment. Safety at the Facility depends upon the manner in which butane is handled as well as the various safety systems/control devices incorporated into the design of the process. Furthermore, comprehensive training is provided to employees, which reinforces the safety policies and procedures of the North Muskegon Terminal.

The facility has fixed inventories of butane.  Butane is received by truck (transports) and stored in two (2) storage vessels. Specifically, liquefied butane is off-loaded by truck for storage under pressure. The butane is then pumped to an injection skid for direct injection into blend grade and premium unleaded gasoline lines primarily feeding the site gasoline truck-loading rack. Injection quantities are controlled via the injection skid and analyzer. In addition to rack blending, the process is also utilized for batch/tank blending based on seasonal gasoline specifications. Process safety controls include excess flow valves, low-melting point (<250 degrees Fahrenheit) fusible elements, fail safe valves, 85% fill shutoff on the vessels, emergency shutoff devices on the system and video display terminal, process area hydrocarbon detectors, thermal and pressure reliefs, and grounding/interlock devices. Access to the North Muskegon Terminal is restricted to authorized employees, management personnel and authorized contractors/visitors.

B. GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC
PREVENTION MEASURES

MPLX's accidental release prevention programs and emergency planning and response programs help effectively manage the hazards posed by regulated substances to employees, the public, and the environment. The covered process is regulated by the EPA RMP regulation 40 CFR Part 68 as well as the OSHA Process Safety Management standard

gation

-Automatic and remotely operated shut-offs to limit release quantities,
-Strategically located valves to isolate leaks,
-Hydrocarbon detectors at key areas to warn of a chemical release and disable the process, and 
-Cooling (fire exposure) water installed near the butane storage vessels and offload area with both auto and manual actuation.

General Emergency Response

-Emergency alert systems;
-Periodic emergency training for employees;
-Communication systems with local emergency responders and regulatory agencies;
-Emergency drills with Terminal personnel, regulatory agencies, and community emergency responders to enhance response skills and coordination among agencies; and
-Mutual Aid with Local Fire Departments.

Further, the North Muskegon LP Terminal complies with the National Fire Protection Association's (NFPA's) Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Code (NFPA-58) requirements for LP Gas storage. In addition to the presence of appropriate controls to prevent and mitigate possible releases of butane, a Facility Response Plan (FRP)and Emergency Response Action Plan (ERAP) are in place with response activities being coordinated with the Muskegon Charter Township Fire Department, North Muskegon Fire Department, and Muskegon County Emergency Services.

C. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

The North Muskegon Terminal has an excellent record of accident prevention. The terminal maintains records for all significant accidental chemical releases that occur at its facility. There have been no reportable accidents within the past five (5) years resulting from the release of materials covered under the EPA RMP regulation.

D. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

The North Muskegon LP Terminal is identified as a Non-Responding Stationary source and, as such, utilizes outside sources (i.e. Muskegon Charter Township Fire Department) for offensive-type response actions.

The FRP and ERAP are part of a comprehensive response plan identified as "Smart Plan".
